subject: Zipline: notification of new telemetry subprocessor and roster + evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@zipline.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: integrations@zipline.com
Date: 2028-07-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Notification: TelemetryFlow being added as telemetry subprocessor (info + roster attached)

Hi Ben and Marissa,

Following our DPA Appendix process, Zipline is adding a short-lived telemetry partner, TelemetryFlow LLC, to our processing roster to support a performance pilot (non-production telemetry) for a month. I attached a CSV roster extract and the TelemetryFlow DPA appendix for your review. High level:

- Purpose: ephemeral telemetry (performance metrics only), sampled and pseudonymized, retention 30 days.
- Location: EU data centers (Ireland) with onshore caching in US West for low-latency dashboards (no full user identifiers will be persisted in the US cache).
- Access: telemetry engineers at TelemetryFlow, SOC2 Type II reported in 2026 (attestation stub in appendix).

Could you confirm whether Redwood needs any additional notice steps (e.g., updated DPA addendum, onshore fallback confirmation, or evidence package) for this temporary addition? We're aiming to spin up next Monday (2028-07-15).

Attaching: zipline_subprocessor_roster_20280708.csv; telemetryflow_dpa_appendix.pdf

Thanks,
Elena Park
Legal Counsel
Zipline Logistics

--
Attachment stubs: zipline_subprocessor_roster_20280708.csv (CSV, 2KB); telemetryflow_dpa_appendix.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@zipline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-08T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notification: TelemetryFlow being added as telemetry subprocessor (info + roster attached)

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Quick clarifying questions before we engage the privacy/security review:

1) You mention "pseudonymized" — can you confirm whether any raw user identifiers (email, account IDs) will ever be present in the EU dataset that TelemetryFlow receives? If so, are they hashed client-side or server-side?
2) For the US caching layer: will any actionable identifiers be present in the cache, or is it strictly aggregated metrics?
3) Is TelemetryFlow a subcontractor of Zipline or contracted directly by a Zipline subvendor? Who signs the DPA appendix?

Marissa/Kimberly/Priyom — looping you in for next steps on evidence and DPA handling. If we need a DPA addendum or a transient onshore fallback approval, Priyom can advise on the fastest path (procurement/legal).

If it helps, we typically ask for: SOC2 summary + scoping statement, data flow diagram for the telemetry path, and confirmation of re-identification risk controls. For temporary processors we also require a sunset/rollback plan.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@zipline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-07-08T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notification: TelemetryFlow being added as telemetry subprocessor (info + roster attached)

Thanks Elena, Ben — appreciate the early notice. From a Privacy/Product standpoint here are the immediate asks and timeline I'd like to propose:

Action items for Zipline (please provide by EOD Friday 2028-07-12):
- Confirm whether any primary identifiers are ever transmitted. If yes, specify transformation/hashing algorithm and salt handling.
- Provide a simple data flow diagram (high level) showing TelemetryFlow ingress -> EU store -> US cache -> Redwood endpoints (if Redwood will receive telemetry).
- Confirm retention enforcement (how is 30d enforced) and deletion proof for the pilot end date.
- Provide SOC2 summary + scope page (we don't need the full report yet, just the scope that covers telemetry services).

Internal owners:
- Priyom: legal review / DPA addendum (if needed).
- Kimberly: security evidence checklist & onshore cache risk assessment.
- Ben: coordinate rollout timing with the customer and confirm whether Redwood will be directly receiving telemetry (some customers push telemetry into our telemetry ingestion pipeline).

If any of the answers are "yes, Redwood will receive raw identifiers" we will need a DPA addendum signed by Zipline + TelemetryFlow (or contracting flow that shows Zipline is bound in the chain).

Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Product Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Elena Park <elena@zipline.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: integrations@zipline.com
Date: 2028-07-09T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notification: TelemetryFlow being added as telemetry subprocessor (info + roster attached)

Marissa/Ben — answers below and attaching the updated data flow diagram per your ask.

1) No primary identifiers will be in TelemetryFlow's EU store. Client-side SDK hashes account_id with a customer-specific salt before transmission; the salt is held by Zipline only. We will include the hashing note in the appendix.
2) US cache is aggregated counters only (minute-level aggregates, no hashes).
3) TelemetryFlow is contracted directly by Zipline; TelemetryFlow signed the DPA appendix included in the prior email.
4) Retention: TelemetryFlow enforces a TTL and provides deletion logs; they have agreed to a 30-day retention with a snapshot at pilot end showing 0 records older than 30d.

Attached: telemetryflow_dataflow_v1.png (PNG, 45KB) and updated telemetryflow_dpa_appendix.pdf (PDF, 124KB)

If Redwood needs TelemetryFlow to sign anything directly to Redwood, let us know — otherwise Zipline will include the appendix in our addendum and ensure TelemetryFlow is bound by our DPA chain.

Thanks,
Elena

--
Attachment stubs: telemetryflow_dataflow_v1.png (PNG, 45KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Notification: TelemetryFlow being added as telemetry subprocessor (info + roster attached)

Elena — this is helpful, thanks for the quick turnaround and the dataflow. Next steps from Redwood:

1) Kimberly will run the onshore cache risk checklist and confirm whether aggregated minute-level counters are acceptable under our onshore processing policy.
2) Priyom will review the DPA appendix and advise if we require any contractual language directly between Redwood and TelemetryFlow or whether Zipline's chain is sufficient.
3) Assuming no red flags, Ben will confirm a go/no-go for the pilot by EOD Monday 2028-07-11 so you can proceed with the 2028-07-15 start as planned.

Elena — please keep the retention/deletion proof and SOC2 scope ready; if Kimberly or Priyom request additional artifacts we'll let you know. Appreciate the transparent note and the sunset plan attached in the appendix.

Ben Carter
